_doc: Round 4 paint-over (ESCALATION 2) for the drive-9 idle at 144 px: hand-placed pixels on the R4u underlay (d9_post.py with r4_finish.json on raw/R4). Coordinates are sprite pixels on that underlay; r4_paint.py skips the file as STALE if the underlay changes. Each layer's 'why' names the round-3 critic fix it answers.

layers.name: face_base
layers.why: Face critic 2: 'the whites read grey ... no cheek or nose form'; a clean 4-tone face plane (refs' faces are 2-3 clean tones, FC-P35) lit from the upper right, with the near cheek and jaw a step down, so the old stamp's grey and brown specks are gone before the new features go on.

layers.name: fringe
layers.why: Face critic 4 (head and hair): 'split the fringe into 5-7 tapered clumps with 1 px dark gaps'; FC: 'a warm skin shadow under the bangs'. Six locks from an off-centre parting (x 48), unequal lengths, tips at the brow line so the eyes stay clear.

layers.name: brows
layers.why: FC: brows always there; a mid hair tone where the fringe leaves skin.

layers.name: brows_far
layers.why: as brows

layers.name: eye_near
layers.why: Face critic 2: 'a 2-3 px black upper-lash mass with an outer flick, an iris ramp from dark at the top to light at the bottom with a 1 px catchlight, a cooler white'; attractiveness 3: 'lids lowered slightly, eyes on the viewer'. Sized to refs 08/09 (an almond 5-6 px wide, 3 iris rows, whites only at the inner corner): the first 7x6 version with a full two-row lash read as closed, sleepy eyes.

layers.name: eye_far
layers.why: as eye_near; the far eye is foreshortened (iris 2 px, toward the nose so she looks at the camera), its flick lifting to the right

layers.name: blush
layers.why: Face critic 2: 'a 2-tone soft pink blush'; the face must read as two eyes plus blush at 80.

layers.name: nose
layers.why: Face critic 2: 'no cheek or nose form': one warm tick on the nose's shadow side.

layers.name: mouth
layers.why: Attractiveness 3: 'an asymmetric closed smile'; face 2: 'a 1 px darker mouth corner'. A 4 px soft V, the far corner darker (M).

layers.name: strand_face
layers.why: Head and hair 4: 'add 2-3 loose strands that cross the face or the outline': one lock end from the parting falls between the eyes.

layers.name: shoulder_split
layers.why: Body critic 5/6 and first impression: 'the collar forearm lies across the top of the bust and flattens it, so it looks stuck on (a rev-3.5 Never)'. There is no forearm there: the lit décolletage (x 41-49) runs straight into the near shoulder and upper arm (x 36-44, going down-left to the elbow), so the two read as one horizontal limb ending in a 'hand'. A shadow line at the chest-shoulder boundary and the shoulder turned a step darker separate the chest plane from the arm. The lit horizontal strip itself is what reads as a limb, so the near chest (x 41-49) is turned into a side plane stepping into shadow toward the arm, lit only at the neck pit.

layers.name: neckline
layers.why: First impression 1: 'shade the bust into the bodice'; the neckline dips into the cleavage (a sweetheart V) so the chest and the bust read as one form.

layers.name: strands_out
layers.why: Head and hair 4: 'no flyaway strands past the silhouette ... add 2-3 loose strands that cross the face or the outline'. A lock end lifts off the near side and falls.

layers.name: strands_out2
layers.why: as strands_out, far side

layers.name: lock_gaps
layers.why: Head and hair 4: 'no clump separation, no dark gaps between clumps': a 1 px dark gap splits the near side mass into two locks.

layers.name: lock_lights
layers.why: Head and hair 4: 'a hue-shifted ramp ... soft-edged locks': a lit edge on the outer lock, tapering.

layers.name: lock_lights2
layers.why: as lock_lights, inner lock

layers.name: bell_folds
layers.why: Materials 14 and first impression: 'bust and sleeves read as pillow blobs': two pipe folds hang from the cuff to the hem of the near bell, each a shadow line with a lit edge beside it.

layers.name: bell_folds_lit
layers.why: as bell_folds

layers.name: bell_folds2
layers.why: as bell_folds

layers.name: lining_folds
layers.why: Mass (F3's bell) and materials 14: the far bell's lining was one flat navy scythe shape; a lit fold ridge and a dark crease give it cloth.

layers.name: lining_folds_dk
layers.why: as lining_folds
